newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says door not closed on fresh PLO contacts.
newsitem.headline: Israel says door not closed on fresh PLO contacts.

text.p: Israel said it had not closed the door on restoring severed contacts with the Palestinian Authority, despite a deepening rift in the wake of a Tel Aviv suicide attack.
A top Palestinian security official said he had stopped security coordination with the Israelis due to what he called Israeli breaches of peace accords.

"We stopped the security coordination as a result of the Israeli contravention of the agreement by establishing settlements," Mohammad Dahlan, head of Preventive Security in Gaza, told a news conference.

But Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's political adviser, Dore Gold, said contacts could resume if the Palestinians fought terrorism and prevented attacks like the Tel Aviv bomb by a member of the Hamas Islamic Resistance Movement, which killed three Israeli women on Friday.

Referring to statements by Netanyahu that Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had given a "green light" to militants to resume attacks against Israel that had been halted for a year, Gold told Reuters:
"The fundamental condition they have to fulfil is security. They have to turn Arafat's green light into a red light. We left the door open."
Asked whether there were contacts between the sides, Gold said: "There may be low level talks on security."

Tensions have been high in recent weeks over Israeli decisions to pull back from a smaller area of the West Bank than the Palestinians expected, and to begin work on building a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Palestinian demonstrators and Israeli troops have fought daily street battles in the West Bank since last week's groundbreaking at the planned settlement.

Israeli forces have been on high alert for suicide attacks and have warned Friday's bomb could be followed by other attacks. Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai charged the Palestinians with not making an effort to fight the militants.
"We could have expected after such a horrendous, murderous attack like this that all the security forces would go out of their way to do the maximum," he told Israel Television.
"And they are not doing this at the required intensity or at full force. We repeat and demand they do it."
Dahlan, speaking at the Gaza news conference before Mordechai made his statement, rejected similar Israeli demands made after a cabinet meeting on Sunday.
"We will not accept or deal with the Israeli conditions and will treat them as if we did not hear them," he said.
In an interview with Palestinian Television Dahlan called the Israeli government "a coalition of murderers and extremists".
He referred to the Tel Aviv bomber Mousa Ghneimat, 28, a Hamas member from the West Bank village of Sourif, as "the martyr who martyred himself in the Tel Aviv operation".
Gold dismissed the comments as "just another example" of "Palestinian statements that are clearly intended to incite and which totally contradict the language of peaceful coexistence".
